headline: Medium data-leakage and cascading-error risks: Notion AI can expose workspace content while the pair lacks direct prompt-injection or write-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a static content-writing repo with no runtime I/O, so it cannot inject directly. Profile B is Notion AI, which reads workspace pages and can surface content into answers, but there is no documented shared clipboard/MCP/filesystem bridge between them. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or workspace content reuse, so the pathway is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies content from agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts
IF agent_b is configured to ingest pasted text as authoritative instructions
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into Notion AI prompts
Add a short prompt prefix instructing Notion AI to treat pasted content as data only
Use a separate review step before reusing any agent_a-generated text
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to copied content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B can access workspace pages and team knowledge base content and sends calls to vendor backends; agent A is a public content-writing repository with no data-touching surface. The pairwise risk is that workspace content can be summarized or exposed through B, but A does not add a second exfiltration path. This exists in default Notion AI use, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent_b is used on pages containing sensitive workspace content
IF the workspace permits Notion AI access to those pages
mitigations: Restrict Notion AI to non-sensitive pages
Remove sensitive pages from shared workspace areas
Review workspace permissions for the invoking user
Turn off AI use on regulated content where possible
requires-engineering: implement data-class tagging and policy enforcement

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write, network, or filesystem capabilities, and agent B explicitly cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface documented between them, so a capability conflict pathway is not plausible.
conditions: IF agent_a gains write or network capabilities not shown in its profile
IF agent_b is granted filesystem or git write permissions
mitigations: Keep agent_a as a read-only reference artifact
Do not grant agent_b additional write scopes
Audit any future capability changes before pairing

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so it may treat agent A-derived text as authoritative if pasted or stored in pages. Agent A can generate prompt-engineering advice, and B can then summarize or act on it without a built-in verification step. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_a-generated guidance is pasted into a Notion page used by agent_b
IF agent_b answers or drafts actions from that page without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Notion AI outputs
Mark agent_a content as untrusted reference material
Ask Notion AI to cite source pages explicitly
Separate draft and approved knowledge bases
requires-engineering: add verification workflows for AI-derived content

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B processes workspace pages and team knowledge base content through vendor backends, creating a compliance surface for whatever data class the workspace holds. Agent A is a public open-source content repo and does not itself add residency or retention obligations. The mismatch is mainly on B's handling of workspace data, so medium is the right level.
conditions: IF the workspace contains regulated or region-bound data
IF Notion AI is enabled on those pages without a matching policy
mitigations: Limit AI use to non-regulated workspaces
Review retention and export settings for the workspace
Confirm regional policy alignment before enabling AI
Document which page classes may be processed by AI
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention controls
